PRIYANSH AGARWAL
THIRD YEAR 
 B.TECH 
COMPUTER ENGINEERING
HTSI INTERVIEW
EXPERIENCE

TABLE OF CONTENTS
1 PREFACE
2 TEST
3 TECHNICAL INTERVIEW
4 HR INTERVIEW
5 RESULT
6 PREP

1   PREFACE 
HTSI(Hilti) was scheduled to visit the campus for internship
drive on 1st September 2022 . The PPT took place on Microsoft
Teams virtually at 3:30 pm for almost 90 minutes.At the end of
the PPT it was declared that the test will be taken on the same
day after the PPT at 6:00 pm.

2   TEST 
The test consisted of MCQs on core CS topics like
DBMS,Computer networking , Operating Systems,Data
structures and one coding question which was this --
https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/program-for-k-most-
recently-used-mru-apps/
MCQs went a bit tough for me especially the networking
part as I was not good in that particular subject.But I took
my time and gave the correct answers.The coding
question was extremely easy it was just left shifting
elements in an array by 1. Also the test is heavily
proctored.Participants have to install Mettl chrome
plugin which enables audio,screen,video proctoring. Ek
bhi popup aaya ya tumne window ya tab change kia toh
the test gets automatically terminated, hence please be
extra careful and don't take the test lightly.

3    TECHNICAL INTERVIEW
       The list of students shortlisted after the test came at
around 9:30 pm the same day and I was glad to see my
name.My interview was scheduled the very next day at
2:00 pm. i.e 2nd September 2022.
        At the start of my interview I was greeted by the
interviewer , I introduced myself and then he introduced
himself (never do this mistake...always let the interviewer
speak first and then only you speak :) ).Always remember
try steering the interview into a direction when you are
introducing yourself.Since I was well-versed in android
development and had confidently studied my projects I
steered the interview completely towards android and
away from DSA :) . The interviewer became very
interested in my knowledge about android and started
asking me questions about my projects. I explained him
one of my projects,the tech stack used and the reason
why I was using the particular tech stack.

In my opinion , the game changer for me was when I
told him I'd developed all my apps following a standard
architecture.That is when, he started questioning me a
lot about what architecture i've used and how does it
benefit my app and I was able to explain him each and
every point related to my project and also he told me to
open my android studio and run my app which
successfully worked.
         He then started asking me Kotlin vs Java specific
questions which were very easy as he himself didn't have
much knowledge about kotlin and was curious about
hearing my take on it. The interviewer interviewed me on
my project for about 43mins as far as I can remember
and then he finally shifted to DSA.
        He asked me first which data structures I know, I told
him graphs,stack,trees,queues,......etc.He then told
me,"Can you explain me what do you know about a binary
tree as a data structure?".I explained him what I
knew.Then he told me to state all types of tree
traversals.Then he told me to implement inorder tree
traversal by writing a pseudocode.
        I was quite happy as I thought it had already been
50mins since the interview started and I thought this was
the last question.

So I started with drawing a random tree and started
explaining my approach . (Always explain your approach
before giving the answer no matter how easy the
question is as it shows your explanation and
understanding skills). As I was writing the pseudocode,he
cut me and told me to find an element in the tree and if
found return true else false. I found this easy and wrote a
pseudocode for it and immediately realised how stupid I
was because the next thing interviewer tells me is that
"your code correctly finds an element in the tree but I
want it to traverse in an inorder fashion while searching
for the element !!".
       I was honestly quite exhausted at this point and
hence I panicked a bit.Always remember never stay quite
during the interview always keep saying what you think
and what you know and explain your approach in detail.
So I started with what I knew and slowly explained my
approach and the interviewer also helped me a lot in
between because I was fumbling a lot.As I recall it now , I
remember how ridiculously easy the question was but I
couldn't think straight because I was so exhausted at that
point.But eventually in 2-3 mins I gave him the correct
answer and he was quite happy with the way I
approached the problem since I was explaining each and
every step with great detail.

Still the interview wasn't done.He then asked me
OOPs oriented questions which were mixed with
Java.Eg:How does inheritance work and how would
you implement it in Java. These questions were
very easy and I was able to answer all of them
easily.He then finally asked if I had any questions
for him .I asked him what work is the company doing
in the app dev space and specifically in
android.Unfortunately he wasn't part of the app
dev space but still he told me a lot about the on-
track gen3 app which the company had just
launched and what tech stack is used and what are
future plans for the company and how has his
experience been so far in the company. Always ask
questions in the end and try keeping it one
technical question and one interviewer based
question.
       The results came after I guess 30 40 mins and I
was selected for the HR round. In my head , I knew
that the most difficult part is now going to begin as
this particular company is known for keeping a very
strict HR round unlike others.

4    HR INTERVIEW
     HR round started at around 4:00 pm. I was greeted
by the interviewer who congratulated me for
successfully clearing the technical round.
        He first introduced himself and his role in the
company. He then asked me to introduce myself.I
introduced myself about my schooling and everything
non-technical about me. He then asked me to tell
everything I know about Hilti. I told him all the things
that I knew and he seemed satisfied. 
        He then asked me the famous HR question ," Why
Hilti?". I told him that it's a product based company
and explained him why working for a product based
company meant more interesting tech will be involved
which means there's more work and hence more to
learn. I also told him about the company's trust in
their employees since the whole internship drive was
undertaken by all the newly-hired employees.

This shows that the company has a good work-culture  
and trust among their workers.
      He seemed happy but not satisfied and moved
ahead by asking me a lot about where I was born and
brought up,about my parents' profession. So I told
him about how I am currently living in Thane. He
abruptly cut me off and told me how happy he was to
finally talk to a Thanekar.We straight up talked for 5
mins  we started bonding on Thane  .     He then
extended his last question by asking , "Why hilti ? Like
why should you join a company jiska business model is
all about selling construction equipments ? Why
should hilti invest in you (tech peeps) ?." I knew with
my 20 mins of interaction with him that he wanted a
practical take on his questions and not standard HR
answers.
      I started with an example of how earlier fridges
were manual with extremely basic features but
nowadays there full fledged apps for controlling a
fridge even when you are thousand kms away from
your home . This increases the market value of that
company's products and also creates a brand value.

I then connected my example and concluded on how a
hardware company can profit a lot if it invests in
software . He seemed satisfied and happy with my
answer.
     He then asked me if I had any questions for him.I
asked him about his role in the company

5    RESULTS
     The results came at around 8:00 pm in the evening and
out of 18 people only 7 were selected and I was happy to see
my name. As I told you earlier,Hilti takes an extremely strict
HR round so please be prepared accordingly.
      After the results, we were told to join a meet with a senior
company official in which he congratulated us for getting
selected.

6    PREP
DSA -->  https://450dsa.com/
CN --> https://www.interviewbit.com/networking-
interview-questions/
DBMS --> https://www.interviewbit.com/dbms-mcq/
SQL --> https://www.sql-practice.com/
OS --> Gate Smashers playlist
      Also for the interview prep in general , I read a lot
of past year interviews and also interacted with
seniors, since there was nothing on GFG archives
based on Hilti. It is very important to know how to
speak in an interview and how to convey your views
and ideas properly to the interviewer in a formal way.
      Also research the company seriously , each and
every bit of information that can impress the HR.

THANK YOU FOR READING
AND ALL THE BEST !!
